### [SEC-IAM-001] IAM policy grants wildcard Action on all resources

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_iam_policy.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The IAM policy grants `Action: "*"` (all AWS actions) on all resources. This gives the attached role full administrative access to every AWS service in the account, violating the principle of least privilege and creating a massive blast radius for any credential compromise.
- **Remediation:** Replace the wildcard `Action` with the specific set of API actions the application actually requires. Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation to derive a minimal policy from CloudTrail activity. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#grant-least-privilege

---

### [SEC-IAM-002] IAM policy grants wildcard Resource scope

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_iam_policy.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The IAM policy sets `Resource: "*"`, granting the permitted actions against every resource in the AWS account. Combined with `Action "*"`, this is effectively an `AdministratorAccess` policy.
- **Remediation:** Scope the `Resource` field to the explicit ARNs of the resources the application needs to access. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#apply-least-privilege-permissions

### [SEC-SG-001] SSH open to the entire internet (0.0.0.0/0)

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_security_group.web`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** Inbound SSH (TCP port 22) is open to the entire internet (`cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]`). This exposes the EC2 instance to brute-force and exploitation attempts from any IP address globally.
- **Remediation:** Remove the public SSH ingress rule. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for shell access without any open inbound ports. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/ec2-controls.html#ec2-13

---

### [SEC-KMS-001] RDS instance storage is not encrypted at rest

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The RDS MySQL instance has `storage_encrypted = false`. All data at rest is stored unencrypted. Fails CIS AWS Benchmark 2.3.1 and AWS Security Hub FSBP RDS.3.
- **Remediation:** Set `storage_encrypted = true`. To use a CMK, set `kms_key_id`. Encryption must be configured at creation time. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html

---

### [SEC-SM-001] RDS master credentials not managed by Secrets Manager

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The RDS instance defines `username = "admin"` inline with no password backed by `aws_secretsmanager_secret` or `aws_ssm_parameter`. Hardcoding or omitting credentials from managed secrets means the password appears in the Terraform state file in plaintext.
- **Remediation:** Create an `aws_secretsmanager_secret` + `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` to store the master password. Enable automatic rotation. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/hardcoded-db-creds.html

### [SEC-S3-001] S3 bucket missing public access block — block_public_acls not enforced

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` resource is defined. `block_public_acls` is not explicitly enforced, allowing a future ACL change to inadvertently expose bucket objects publicly.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` resource with `block_public_acls = true`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html

---

### [SEC-S3-002] S3 bucket missing public access block — block_public_policy not enforced

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** `block_public_policy` is not configured. A permissive bucket policy (e.g., `Principal: "*"`) could be applied and publicly expose bucket contents.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` resource with `block_public_policy = true`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html

---

### [SEC-S3-003] S3 bucket missing public access block — ignore_public_acls not enforced

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** `ignore_public_acls` is not configured. Existing public ACLs on the bucket or its objects continue to grant public access.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` resource with `ignore_public_acls = true`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html

---

### [SEC-S3-004] S3 bucket missing public access block — restrict_public_buckets not enforced

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** `restrict_public_buckets` is not configured. Cross-account or public access through bucket policies is not prevented at the S3 infrastructure level.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` resource with `restrict_public_buckets = true` (all four settings set to `true`). Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/configuring-block-public-access-bucket.html

---

### [SEC-S3-005] S3 bucket has no server-side encryption configuration

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration` resource is defined. The IaC does not explicitly declare an encryption configuration, making the protection implicit and unverifiable through code review.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration` resource with SSE-KMS using a customer-managed key, or at minimum SSE-S3 (AES256). Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html

### [SEC-CT-001] No AWS CloudTrail trail defined

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `N/A (no aws_cloudtrail resource defined)`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No AWS CloudTrail trail is defined anywhere in the IaC. Without CloudTrail, there is no audit record of API calls, IAM changes, resource modifications, or security-relevant events. Violates CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark 3.1.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_cloudtrail` resource with `is_multi_region_trail = true`, `enable_log_file_validation = true`, and a `cloud_watch_logs_group_arn`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-controls.html

### [REL-MAZ-001] RDS instance deployed without Multi-AZ

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The production RDS instance (prod-db, MySQL 8.0) has `multi_az = false`. In the event of an AZ or hardware failure, the database will be completely unavailable with no automatic failover.
- **Remediation:** Set `multi_az = true` on `aws_db_instance.main`. Also add subnets in separate AZs to the subnet group. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html

---

### [REL-BKP-001] RDS automated backups disabled and no final snapshot on deletion

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** `backup_retention_period = 0` (automated backups disabled) AND `skip_final_snapshot = true` (no snapshot on deletion). Any data loss event would be permanent and unrecoverable.
- **Remediation:** Set `backup_retention_period` to at minimum `7` for production. Set `skip_final_snapshot = false` and provide `final_snapshot_identifier`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.Enabling.html

---

### [REL-SPOF-001] Single EC2 instance with no Auto Scaling Group

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** A single EC2 instance is deployed in production with no Auto Scaling Group. Instance failure results in complete application unavailability with no automatic recovery.
- **Remediation:** Replace with `aws_launch_template` + `aws_autoscaling_group` with `min_size >= 2` across at least two AZs. Add an ALB. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html

---

### [REL-SPOF-002] Single NAT Gateway creates AZ-level single point of failure

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_nat_gateway.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** Only a single NAT Gateway in a single AZ. All private subnet instances depend on this gateway. An AZ failure cuts all private subnet internet connectivity.
- **Remediation:** Provision one NAT Gateway per AZ used by private subnets. Update private route tables per AZ. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html#nat-gateway-basics

### [NET-SUB-001] Application EC2 instance placed in public subnet

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The application EC2 instance is placed directly in the public subnet. The `outputs.tf` file exposes `instance_public_ip`, confirming a public IP is expected. Application compute should never sit on the internet-facing tier.
- **Remediation:** Move `aws_instance.app` to `aws_subnet.private`. Place an ALB in the public subnet as the sole internet-facing entry point. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-example-web-database-servers.html

### [NET-RT-001] No route tables defined — Internet Gateway and NAT Gateway are orphaned

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_vpc.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No `aws_route_table`, `aws_route`, or `aws_route_table_association` resources are defined. All subnets fall back to the implicit main route table (local-only). The Internet Gateway and NAT Gateway are both orphaned with no routes pointing to them.
- **Remediation:** Create separate `aws_route_table` resources per tier: public (`0.0.0.0/0` → IGW), private (`0.0.0.0/0` → NAT), isolated (local only). Associate each to the corresponding subnets. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-tutorials-intro.html

### [NET-SGP-001] Security group with public SSH/HTTP attached to both EC2 and RDS

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_security_group.web`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The security group allows inbound SSH (TCP/22) from `0.0.0.0/0`. The same security group is attached to the RDS instance, meaning the database inherits HTTP/80 and SSH/22 ingress rules from the internet.
- **Remediation:** Remove the public SSH ingress rule and adopt SSM Session Manager. Create a dedicated security group for RDS allowing only MySQL/3306 from the application SG.

### [OPS-TAG-001] AWS provider has no default_tags block

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `provider.aws`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The Terraform AWS provider block defines no `default_tags` block. Without provider-level default tags, tags will inevitably be missed on most resources (VPC, subnet, security group, NAT gateway, RDS, S3 bucket, IAM role all carry no tags).
- **Remediation:** Add a `default_tags` block to the provider including `Environment`, `Project`, `Owner`, and `ManagedBy`. Reference: https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#default_tags

---

### [OPS-MON-001] No CloudWatch alarms for the EC2 instance

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` is defined for the EC2 instance. Without `CPUUtilization` or `StatusCheckFailed` alarms, degraded performance or outages go undetected until users report them.
- **Remediation:** Define at minimum: `CPUUtilization >= 80%` for 3 consecutive 5-minute periods, and `StatusCheckFailed >= 1`. Both should publish to SNS. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/US_AlarmAtThresholdEC2.html

---

### [OPS-MON-002] No CloudWatch alarms for the RDS instance

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` resources for RDS. With only 20 GB allocated storage, a missing `FreeStorageSpace` alarm is especially dangerous — the database can run out of space silently.
- **Remediation:** Add CloudWatch alarms for `FreeStorageSpace < 5 GB`, `CPUUtilization >= 80%`, and `DatabaseConnections` threshold. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-cloudwatch.html

---

### [OPS-LOG-001] VPC Flow Logs completely absent

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `aws_vpc.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** VPC Flow Logs are completely absent. No network-level visibility for incident investigation, anomaly detection, or compliance mandates (CIS, PCI DSS, SOC 2).
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_flow_log` resource targeting the VPC, publishing to CloudWatch Logs with a retention policy. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-cwl.html

---

### [OPS-LOG-002] No CloudWatch Log Groups defined anywhere

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Resource:** `N/A (no aws_cloudwatch_log_group defined)`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** There are no `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resources anywhere. No application logging infrastructure, no log retention policy, no ability to create metric filters. CloudWatch log groups without a retention policy default to Never Expire, causing unbounded cost growth.
- **Remediation:** Define at minimum one CloudWatch log group per service component with `retention_in_days` (90 days for production, 30 for non-production). Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/Working-with-log-groups-and-streams.html

### [SEC-CT-002] CloudTrail does not cover multiple regions

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `N/A`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** Multi-region trail coverage is not enabled. A single-region trail misses API activity in other regions including global services such as IAM and STS.
- **Remediation:** When creating the `aws_cloudtrail` resource, set `is_multi_region_trail = true`.

### [SEC-CT-003] CloudTrail log file validation not enabled

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `N/A`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** CloudTrail log file validation is not enabled. Log file validation creates digitally signed digest files to detect tampering.
- **Remediation:** When creating the `aws_cloudtrail` resource, set `enable_log_file_validation = true`.

- **Resource:** `N/A`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** CloudTrail is not integrated with CloudWatch Logs. No real-time monitoring or alerting on security-relevant API events.
- **Remediation:** Set `cloud_watch_logs_group_arn` and `cloud_watch_logs_role_arn` on the `aws_cloudtrail` resource.

### [SEC-SG-002] Security group allows unrestricted outbound traffic

- **Resource:** `aws_security_group.web`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The egress rule allows all outbound traffic. If the EC2 instance is compromised, unrestricted egress enables data exfiltration and C2 communication.

### [COST-NAT-001] NAT Gateway deployed unconditionally for all environments

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_nat_gateway.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** A NAT Gateway is deployed unconditionally for every environment. In ap-northeast-1 a NAT Gateway costs ~$0.062/hr (~$45/month) plus $0.062/GB in data-processing fees. The `var.environment` variable is never used to control NAT count.
- **Remediation:** Use `count = var.environment == "production" ? 1 : 0` on `aws_nat_gateway.main` and `aws_eip.nat` so non-production environments can eliminate the gateway. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-pricing.html

### [COST-NAT-002] No VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3/DynamoDB — S3 traffic billed through NAT

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_vpc.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3 or DynamoDB. S3 traffic from private subnets routes through NAT incurring per-GB charges ($0.062/GB). Gateway Endpoints are free.
- **Remediation:** Add `aws_vpc_endpoint` resources with `service_name` for S3 (type `Gateway`) and associate with the private route table.

### [COST-S3-001] S3 bucket has no lifecycle configuration

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The S3 bucket has no lifecycle configuration. Data accumulates in S3 Standard ($0.025/GB/month in ap-northeast-1) indefinitely.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration` resource with transitions to S3-IA or Glacier and expiration for incomplete multipart uploads.

---

### [COST-S3-002] S3 versioning enabled with no noncurrent-version expiration rule

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket_versioning.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** S3 versioning is enabled but there is no lifecycle rule to expire noncurrent object versions. Every overwrite creates a noncurrent version billed at full S3 Standard rates indefinitely, potentially multiplying storage costs 2–5×.
- **Remediation:** Add a `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` rule (e.g., expire after 30–90 days) and a `NoncurrentVersionTransition` rule.

### [COST-TAG-001] EC2 instance missing cost allocation tags

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The EC2 instance carries only a `Name` tag. `Environment`, `Team`, and `Project` tags are absent across all resources. Without cost allocation tags, spend cannot be attributed by project, team, or environment.
- **Remediation:** Define a `locals` block with `common_tags` and apply `tags = merge(local.common_tags, {...})` on every taggable resource. Activate keys as Cost Allocation Tags in the Billing console.

- **Resource:** `aws_db_subnet_group.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The DB subnet group includes only a single subnet in a single AZ. AWS requires subnets in at least two AZs for Multi-AZ. The current configuration structurally prevents Multi-AZ.

### [NET-VPC-003] VPC DNS settings not explicitly configured

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_subnet_group.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** `aws_db_subnet_group.main` references only a single subnet in a single AZ. RDS requires a subnet group spanning at least two AZs for Multi-AZ.
- **Remediation:** Add private/isolated subnets in at least two AZs to `subnet_ids` in `aws_db_subnet_group.main`.

---

### [NET-NACL-001] No custom Network ACLs defined — default permissive NACLs in use

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_vpc.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No `aws_network_acl` resources are defined. All subnets use the default permissive NACL. Without custom NACLs, lateral movement within subnet tiers cannot be blocked at the network layer.
- **Remediation:** Define custom NACLs per subnet tier allowing only necessary traffic. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nacl-examples.html

---

### [NET-SGP-002] RDS instance uses EC2 security group permitting internet-sourced traffic

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** `aws_db_instance.main` uses the same security group as the EC2 instance, which allows HTTP/80 and SSH/22 from `0.0.0.0/0`. The database should only accept connections from the app tier on port 3306.
- **Remediation:** Create a dedicated `aws_security_group` for RDS allowing only inbound TCP/3306 from `aws_security_group.web`.

---

### [OPS-TAG-002] Most resources carry no tags

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app, aws_vpc.main, aws_security_group.web, aws_db_instance.main, aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The majority of resources have no tags. VPC, security group, RDS, S3 bucket, NAT Gateway, and IAM role carry zero tags. Missing `Environment`, `Project`, and `Owner` tags breaks cost allocation and incident response.
- **Remediation:** Once `default_tags` is added to the provider (OPS-TAG-001), all resources will inherit common tags automatically.

---

### [OPS-OPS-001] SSH port 22 open to internet on production instance

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_security_group.web`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** Port 22 (SSH) is open to `0.0.0.0/0`. For a production deployment, interactive access should use SSM Session Manager, which provides a complete audit trail of session commands and eliminates inbound firewall rules.
- **Remediation:** Remove the SSH ingress rule. Attach `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` to the IAM role. Configure VPC endpoints for SSM to avoid routing traffic through the internet.

---

### [OPS-LOG-003] No AWS CloudTrail trail defined

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `N/A (no aws_cloudtrail defined)`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No AWS CloudTrail trail. All management-plane API calls are unrecorded beyond the default 90-day event history. No metric filters or alarms can be created for critical API events.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_cloudtrail` resource delivering events to S3 and CloudWatch Logs, with log file validation and multi-region coverage.

---

### [OPS-CFG-001] No AWS Config rules or conformance packs

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `N/A (no aws_config_config_rule defined)`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No AWS Config rules or conformance packs. No automated detection of configuration drift (public S3 bucket, unencrypted RDS, missing VPC flow logs, etc.).
- **Remediation:** Enable AWS Config recording and deploy a conformance pack. Relevant managed rules: `vpc-flow-logs-enabled`, `rds-multi-az-support`, `rds-storage-encrypted`, `s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited`.

---

### [PERF-DB-001] RDS storage type defaults to gp2 — performance cliff risk

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** RDS `storage_type` defaults to `gp2`. For 20 GiB, gp2 provisions only 60 IOPS baseline with burst credits. Once credits exhaust, throughput falls to the baseline — a performance cliff. gp3 delivers 3,000 IOPS baseline at 20% lower cost per GiB.
- **Remediation:** Add `storage_type = "gp3"` to `aws_db_instance.main`. No downtime required. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html#migrate-to-gp3

---

### [PERF-COMP-001] EC2 instance uses Intel x86 — Graviton2 offers better price-performance

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** EC2 instance is `t3.micro` (Intel x86_64). The `t4g.micro` (AWS Graviton2) offers up to 20% lower price for equivalent or better CPU performance.
- **Remediation:** Evaluate `t4g.micro` after confirming the AMI supports ARM64. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/burstable-performance-instances.html

---

### [PERF-COMP-002] RDS uses db.t3.micro — Graviton2 offers lower cost and no burst credit exhaustion

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** RDS instance uses `db.t3.micro` (Intel x86_64). The `db.t4g.micro` (Graviton2) offers ~20% lower cost for MySQL 8.0 and runs Unlimited burst by default, eliminating credit exhaustion risk.
- **Remediation:** Change `instance_class` to `db.t4g.micro`. MySQL 8.0 is fully supported on `db.t4g`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.DBInstanceClass.Types.html

---

### [PERF-CACHE-001] No caching layer — all reads hit RDS directly

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No ElastiCache cluster is defined. The application connects directly to RDS for every request. For a read-heavy production workload, all reads hit the database, resulting in higher latency and elevated DB CPU.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_elasticache_replication_group` (Redis/Valkey) in a private subnet for application-level caching. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WorkingWithElastiCache.html

---

### [PERF-DB-002] No RDS read replica — all query traffic hits the single primary

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No RDS read replica configured. All query traffic hits the single primary instance, constraining read throughput and risking read/write contention.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_db_instance` with `replicate_source_db = aws_db_instance.main.identifier` in a second AZ. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html

---

### [SUS-GRAV-001] EC2 instance uses Intel x86 — Graviton2 is more energy-efficient

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** EC2 instance uses `t3.micro` (Intel x86_64). The `t4g.micro` (Graviton2) delivers up to 20% better price-performance and is more energy-efficient. In ap-northeast-1, `t3.micro` is ~$0.0152/hr vs `t4g.micro` ~$0.0084/hr — approximately 45% annual savings.
- **Remediation:** Change `instance_type` to `t4g.micro`. Ensure AMI supports ARM64. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/ec2-view-recommendations.html

---

### [SUS-GRAV-002] RDS uses Intel x86 — Graviton2 is more energy-efficient

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** RDS instance uses `db.t3.micro` (Intel x86_64) with MySQL 8.0. `db.t4g.micro` (Graviton2) fully supports MySQL 8.0 and is ~20% cheaper and more energy-efficient. In ap-northeast-1, `db.t3.micro` is ~$0.026/hr vs `db.t4g.micro` ~$0.016/hr — ~38% annual savings.
- **Remediation:** Change `instance_class` to `db.t4g.micro`. MySQL 8.0 is fully supported. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.DBInstanceClass.Support.html

---

### [SUS-STOR-001] S3 bucket accumulates objects indefinitely — no lifecycle policy

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** The S3 bucket has no lifecycle policy. Objects accumulate indefinitely consuming data-center capacity and energy beyond the data's useful life. Versioning multiplies stored object count with no expiry rules.
- **Remediation:** Add `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration` to transition to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days, expire non-current versions after 90 days, and remove incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.

---

### [SUS-NET-001] No S3 VPC Gateway Endpoint — S3 traffic traverses NAT Gateway unnecessarily

- **Severity:** WARNING
- **Resource:** `aws_nat_gateway.main`
- **File:** `examples/terraform/main.tf`
- **Details:** No S3 VPC Gateway Endpoint. S3 traffic from private subnets traverses the NAT Gateway, increasing data-path hops, energy use, and data-transfer costs ($0.045/GB in Tokyo). A Gateway Endpoint routes traffic directly over the AWS backbone at no charge.
- **Remediation:** Add `aws_vpc_endpoint` resources of type `Gateway` for S3 and DynamoDB, attached to the private route table.

## Recommendations

> These improvements can further increase architecture maturity.

---

### [SEC-SM-002] Configure automatic secret rotation for RDS credentials

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **Details:** No automatic secret rotation is configured. Static long-lived credentials significantly raise the risk exposure window after compromise.
- **Remediation:** Configure automatic rotation on the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource. Set a schedule of 30–90 days. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html

---

### [SEC-KMS-002] Use SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key for the S3 data bucket

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **Details:** For a production data bucket, SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key is preferred as it provides key access policies and CloudTrail audit logs of key usage.
- **Remediation:** Use SSE-KMS in the `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration` resource.

---

### [SEC-IAM-004] Enable IAM Access Analyzer to generate least-privilege policies

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_iam_policy.app`
- **Details:** No IAM Access Analyzer is referenced. It can automatically generate a minimal least-privilege policy from CloudTrail activity.
- **Remediation:** Enable IAM Access Analyzer (`aws_accessanalyzer_analyzer`) in the account.

---

### [COST-EC2-001] Consider a Compute Savings Plan for baseline EC2 usage

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** EC2 instance uses On-Demand pricing with no commitment discount. A 1-year Compute Savings Plan provides ~34% savings; a 3-year plan up to ~60%.
- **Remediation:** Purchase a Compute Savings Plan covering baseline EC2 usage. Use AWS Cost Explorer Savings Plans Recommendations.

---

### [COST-EC2-002] Single EC2 instance runs at full capacity during off-peak hours

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** No Auto Scaling Group means the instance runs at full capacity even during off-peak hours, paying for idle compute.
- **Remediation:** Replace with an `aws_autoscaling_group` backed by an `aws_launch_template` with target-tracking scaling and Spot Instances for fault-tolerant tiers.

---

### [COST-RDS-001] Non-production RDS runs 24/7 — consider off-hours stop schedules

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **Details:** RDS instance deployed identically regardless of `environment` value. Non-production environments could use off-hours stop schedules to save ~70%.
- **Remediation:** Use `var.environment` to conditionally stop the RDS via EventBridge Scheduler for non-production. Consider Aurora Serverless v2 for variable workloads.

---

### [REL-DR-003] No RTO/RPO targets documented in resource tags or configuration

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** No RTO or RPO targets are documented in tags or configuration. Without documented targets it is impossible to verify the architecture meets business continuity requirements.
- **Remediation:** Add tags such as `RTO = "4h"` and `RPO = "1h"` to critical resources. Use AWS Resilience Hub to assess resiliency. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/resilience-hub/latest/userguide/resiliency-policies.html

---

### [REL-BKP-003] No centralised AWS Backup plan for RDS and EC2

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **Details:** No centralised AWS Backup plan covering RDS and EC2 EBS volumes. AWS Backup provides unified backup with cross-region copy and immutable vaults.
- **Remediation:** Create `aws_backup_plan` with daily backup rule and `aws_backup_selection` covering RDS and EC2. Add `copy_action` for a second region.

---

### [REL-ASG-002] If an ASG is introduced, connect scaling policies to CloudWatch alarms

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** If an ASG is introduced, ensure scaling policies are connected to CloudWatch alarms. Without alarm-driven policies the ASG will not respond dynamically to traffic spikes.
- **Remediation:** Define `aws_autoscaling_policy` with target tracking and `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` resources for scale-out and scale-in.

---

### [NET-VPC-004] Add a free S3 VPC Gateway Endpoint to eliminate NAT processing costs

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **Details:** No `aws_vpc_endpoint` for Amazon S3. All S3 traffic from private subnets traverses the NAT Gateway, incurring per-GB NAT processing charges.
- **Remediation:** Add `aws_vpc_endpoint` for `com.amazonaws.<region>.s3` (type `Gateway`) and associate with both route tables. Gateway endpoints are free.

---

### [NET-VPC-005] Add interface VPC endpoints for SSM and Secrets Manager

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_vpc.main`
- **Details:** No interface VPC endpoints for SSM, Secrets Manager, or other control-plane services. If NAT Gateway is unavailable, private-subnet instances lose access to these services.
- **Remediation:** Create `aws_vpc_endpoint` resources for `com.amazonaws.<region>.ssm`, `ssmmessages`, `ec2messages`, and `secretsmanager` with `private_dns_enabled = true`.

---

### [NET-SGP-003] Adopt SSM Session Manager to eliminate SSH dependency

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_security_group.web`
- **Details:** Infrastructure relies on SSH for instance access, requiring an open inbound port and key management. SSM Session Manager provides shell access with zero open inbound ports.
- **Remediation:** Remove SSH ingress rule. Attach `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` to the IAM role and create SSM VPC endpoints.

---

### [NET-RT-002] Define separate route tables per network tier

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_vpc.main`
- **Details:** Separate route tables per network tier are not defined. Without tier-specific route tables, routing isolation between public, private, and isolated tiers cannot be enforced.
- **Remediation:** Define three `aws_route_table` resources (public/private/isolated) and associate each subnet to its corresponding route table.

---

### [OPS-OBS-001] Create a CloudWatch dashboard for operational visibility

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `N/A (no aws_cloudwatch_dashboard defined)`
- **Details:** There is no CloudWatch dashboard. A unified dashboard combining EC2, RDS, and NAT Gateway metrics gives operators a real-time view of system health during incidents.
- **Remediation:** Define an `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` with widgets for all key compute and data resources.

---

### [OPS-OPS-002] Store RDS master password in Secrets Manager

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **Details:** The RDS username `admin` is hardcoded and the password is unmanaged. Configuration values should be stored in SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager.
- **Remediation:** Store DB password in Secrets Manager and reference with data source. Use `manage_master_user_password = true` for native RDS Secrets Manager integration.

---

### [PERF-CDN-001] Add a CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket.data`
- **Details:** No CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket. If this bucket serves static assets, every request traverses the internet to the ap-northeast-1 origin.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_cloudfront_distribution` with an S3 origin. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/GettingStartedCreateDistro.html

---

### [PERF-SCALE-001] Replace single EC2 instance with an Auto Scaling Group

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** Single EC2 instance with no ASG. Cannot scale out under traffic spikes, leading to latency degradation and potential outages.
- **Remediation:** Replace with an `aws_autoscaling_group` backed by `aws_launch_template` and a `TargetTrackingScaling` policy. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html

---

### [PERF-DB-003] Add RDS Proxy to protect against connection exhaustion

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_db_instance.main`
- **Details:** No `aws_db_proxy` (RDS Proxy). Future Lambda functions connecting to this RDS instance could exhaust MySQL `max_connections` on `db.t3.micro` (66 connections).
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_db_proxy` targeting `aws_db_instance.main` with `engine_family = MYSQL` and Secrets Manager auth. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-planning.html

---

### [SUS-SCHED-001] Implement off-hours scheduling for non-production EC2 and RDS

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app, aws_db_instance.main`
- **Details:** No Instance Scheduler tags or schedule-aware logic. Non-production EC2 and RDS running 24/7 waste energy. A 12-hour/5-day schedule reduces runtime to ~35% of full-time, cutting energy use ~65% for those environments.
- **Remediation:** Deploy the AWS Instance Scheduler and apply schedule tags when `var.environment != production`. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managedservices/latest/userguide/ams-resource-scheduler.html

---

### [SUS-STOR-002] Add noncurrent-version expiration rule to manage versioned S3 objects

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_s3_bucket_versioning.data`
- **Details:** S3 versioning is enabled but no lifecycle rule manages non-current versions. Every overwrite retains a version in S3 Standard indefinitely, silently growing storage footprint.
- **Remediation:** Add a lifecycle rule with `noncurrent_version_expiration` (90 days) and `noncurrent_version_transition` to Glacier Instant Retrieval after 30 days.

---

### [SUS-SRVLS-001] Evaluate serverless or Fargate Spot for intermittent workloads

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** If the workload is intermittent or event-driven, migrating to Lambda (ARM64) or ECS Fargate with Spot capacity would eliminate idle compute and reduce energy proportional to actual utilisation.
- **Remediation:** Evaluate whether the application logic can be repackaged as Lambda (`architectures = [arm64]`) or ECS Fargate with Spot. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/foundation-arch.html

---

### [SUS-STOR-003] Create a DLM policy to manage EBS snapshot lifecycle

- **Severity:** INFO
- **Resource:** `aws_instance.app`
- **Details:** No AWS Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) policy for EBS snapshots. Without DLM, EBS snapshots accumulate indefinitely consuming energy and accruing storage cost.
- **Remediation:** Add an `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` creating daily snapshots and retaining the last 7 (production) or 3 (non-production) copies.
